feedback:
Pre-race review of the sensor spacing refinement: sensor x positions from -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04 to -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03. Everything else stays at the iteration 7 values (sensor_size 0.016, kp 3.0, kd 0.8, ki 0, base_speed 1.0, line_loss last_direction, weights -2, -1, 0, 1, 2). Iteration 7 (sensor_size 0.016) is the best raced design at 633.93. Its slalom progress rose from 0.215 to 0.371 with the oval still at 20 of 20, which is the evidence that sensing is the slalom lever. Iteration 5 and iteration 6 showed that kp and ki changes did not move slalom, so spacing is the lever to test next.

The candidate is valid. All positions are inside the x and y limits, the weights are unchanged, and sensor_size 0.016 is an allowed option. It changes one variable from the best design, so the race isolates spacing.

One point for the Optimizer to note: the weights stay fixed while the sensors move closer together. The steering signal per metre of tape offset therefore rises by roughly 0.04/0.03, about 1.33 times, so the effective steering gain goes up even though kp is unchanged. This matches the s-bend and oval risk. Iteration 5 showed that more effective steering gain cost s-bend finishes, so a narrower array could do the same.

Do not treat the expected slalom gain as measured. Once the race reports, read it as follows. If slalom progress rises above 0.37 with the oval at 20 of 20 and s-bend finishes at 14 or more, keep the narrower spacing. If s-bend finishes fall below 14 or the oval drops, return to the iteration 7 spacing (0.02 steps) with sensor_size 0.016. If slalom stays flat near 0.37, bend geometry or base_speed is the limit, so test base_speed 0.8 to 0.9.
requested_changes: If slalom progress rises above 0.37 and the oval holds 20 of 20 with s-bend finishes at 14 or more, keep geometry.sensor_positions at x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03 with sensor_size 0.016, kp 3.0, kd 0.8, ki 0, and test controller.base_speed 0.9 on slalom, since iteration 7 showed sensing is the slalom lever.

If s-bend finishes drop below 14 of 20 or the oval drops below 20 of 20, return geometry.sensor_positions to x = -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04 and keep sensor_size 0.016, because iteration 7 (the best raced design at 633.93) is the base to beat.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.3 on the oval with the narrower array, reduce controller.kp from 3.0 to about 2.7 instead of changing spacing again, because the narrower array raises the effective steering gain by about 1.33 times with fixed weights.
